title: Approximate Differential Privacy of the $\ell_2$ Mechanism
page_convention: PDF pages 1–16 equal internal printed pages
scoped_summary: A valid uniform unit-l2-sensitivity Laplace calibration disproves the near-optimal baseline assertion at d=100, epsilon=1, delta=1e-5. A separate closed-event endpoint mismatch causes a false negative in the printed checker. Interior cap geometry, moment and sampler checks found no substantive issue within the checked assumptions.
limitations: No author code execution or benchmark/timing reproduction.
OpenReview-only attachments unavailable in source preparation.
Current released code is not established as experiment-time code.
Floating-point rigor and exhaustive arbitrary-parameter implementation behavior were not verified.

problems.title: Laplace baseline near-optimality is false under unit l2 sensitivity
problems.claim: Section 4.2 uses smallest possible scales and footnote 2 describes the minimum Laplace scale as negligibly smaller than sqrt(d)/(epsilon+delta).
problems.location: PDF p.8 Section4.2, footnote2; pp.15–16 LemmaA.2; laplace.py get_laplace_sigma.
assumptions: Any statistic with l2 sensitivity at most one
Independent Laplace coordinates with scale b
For all ordered adjacent displacements v with ||v||2<=1
problems.check: For independent Li=(|Zi-vi|-|Zi|)/b, |Li|<=ai=|vi|/b; E Li=ai+exp(-ai)-1<=ai^2/2; sum ai^2<=1/b^2. Bounded-variable exponential moment and Chernoff imply P(L>epsilon)<=exp[-b^2(epsilon-1/(2b^2))^2/2].
problems.result: Candidate is (1,1e-5)-DP: upper bound 6.113567966371413e-6. Its MSE=5000 versus paper MSE=19999.600005999917; ratio0.250005000025.
counterevidence: Printed Laplace calibration is conservative and valid.
Axis argument is relevant under unit l1 sensitivity but does not establish sqrt(d) optimality under l2 sensitivity.
This counterexample does not show Laplace beats l2 or analytic Gaussian, or refute d=7 peak advantage. Figure1 truncates Laplace after d=8.
Current code implements printed calibration; historical code provenance unestablished.
problems.core_dependency: Invalid derivation directly supports optimal-comparator error comparison Section4.2 and minimum-scale characterization Figure5.

correction.statement: Describe existing Laplace baseline as conservatively calibrated. Stated Hoeffding bound gives another sufficient l2-sensitivity calibration, not exact optimum.
correction.verification: Full analytic guarantee plus numeric evaluation; optimized baseline experiment not rerun.

problems.impact: Invalid derivation directly supports optimal-comparator error comparison Section4.2 and minimum-scale characterization Figure5.

problems.title: Closed-event pure-DP endpoint mismatch at d=1
problems.claim: Lemma3.2/Cor3.14 claim probability0 at sigma>=1/epsilon; Algorithms1 and2 disagree at equality.
problems.location: PDF p3 Lemma3.2, p5 Algorithm1/Cor3.14, p6 Algorithm2, p7 Algorithm3; l2.py get_plrv_1_upper_bound/get_plrv_2_lower_bound.
assumptions: d=1, epsilon=1, sigma=1; centers0 and1; unit sensitivity
0 < delta < 1/2 for the executable Algorithm3 false-negative claim; its preliminary radius requires tail probability delta/100 > 0.
problems.check: V=(-infinity,0], P0(V)=1/2, P1(V)=1/(2e); actual hockey-stick difference0. Printed Algorithm1 returns1/2 and Algorithm2 returns0.
problems.result: Printed Algorithm3 rejects this valid pure 1-DP mechanism for 0 < delta < 1/2. At delta=0, its preliminary finite-radius truncation cannot achieve zero tail probability; the executable false-negative claim excludes that case.
counterevidence: False negative only, no unsafe privacy acceptance established.
Current l2.py returns0 for both terms at equality and hence correct combined difference; no attribution of printed false negative to current code.
problems.core_dependency: Local endpoint, no demonstrated failure of interior core privacy bound.

correction.statement: Overall checker can return true directly for sigma>=1/epsilon by pureDP; closed-event lemmas must retain d=1 endpoint probabilities, or use a strict event consistently.

problems.impact: Local endpoint, no demonstrated failure of interior core privacy bound.
